rationale: Economically coherent and untested as a pair, but the "partition" justification is weakened by mechanical entanglement — a high act/at shrinks the denominator of ebitda/(at−act), so the two ranks are structurally coupled rather than independent legs, and the construct sits close to the archive's already-strong act/at + ebitda/lt composite.

A legitimate coverage-repair robustness test of the archive's best-alpha signal rather than new economics, but splicing ib into an oancf-based yield mixes two constructs with different accrual content, so a coverage gain will be hard to distinguish from a change in the signal's meaning.

Multi-anchor value composites are a well-worn construction and both anchors have already been interacted with survival-type legs in the archive, so this is a modest measurement-error variant with limited upside information, though it is internally consistent and correctly signed.

The collateral-quality mechanism is the freshest economic content in the batch and is not in the archive, but revt/act is close to the published asset-turnover/quality-value channel (Piotroski, DuPont) and is strongly industry-determined with no industry neutralization, so a positive result may reflect industry composition rather than realizability.

This is essentially the archived One Year Liquidity Surplus Value with the horizon changed from one to three years and lct swapped for lt, an interpolation between two already-tested constructs that the objective explicitly discourages as a cosmetic variant.

A clean and internally consistent decomposition of the archive's dominant alpha channel into its haircut-free component, though che/act overlaps the known cash-holdings premium and the leg will partly reload on the same firm characteristics as the tested che/lct construct.
